newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Kiwi vols jump as spot plunges.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Kiwi vols jump as spot plunges.

text.p: Implied volatilities on New Zealand dollar options leaped on spot's nosedive.
The kiwi dollar slid more than one U.S. cent overnight as long-term investors bailed out, in the latest instalment of a move which has seen it shed around four cents in just a month.

Dealers said one-month vol had jumped around a point to 7.1/8.0 percent from Thursday, though some said trade was thin and the move represented marking-up of volatilities rather than a headlong rush to buy.

"There's not that much going on -- it's more the expectation that no-one really wants to sell vol because spot's moving around, and they've just marked it up," said an options dealer at an Australian bank in London.
The New Zealand dollar was quoted at 65.06/13 U.S. cents at 1032 GMT, compared to 66.00/07 at Thursday's Wellington close. It finished last night in Wellington at 65 cents.
Traders said vols had held up surprisingly well during spot's journey lower in recent weeks, and the overnight move was a delayed reaction to the spot decline.

Farther along the volatility curve, two-month vol was quoted around 0.7 percent higher at 6.7/7.5 percent, with three-month up 0.5 percent at 6.5/7.0 percent and one-year 0.2 percent firmer at 6.3/6.7 percent.
